claims.text: Greg Short (co-founder of Bloom, circa 2020-2021) reports that deploying a coordinated simultaneous multi-channel marketing push — email, SMS, Facebook ads, and meme page ads all going live at the same moment — at the time of a product restock for Bloom's greens powder generated $1.36 million in sales within 12 hours, with a three-person team.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Product had been out of stock for several weeks prior, creating pent-up demand
All marketing channels deployed simultaneously at restock moment
Channels included email, SMS, Facebook ads, and meme page ads

numbers.axis: single-day revenue from coordinated restock launch

anchors.region: team size at time of launch

bounded_by: Single data point from one brand; no comparison to non-simultaneous channel deployment or smaller team conditions

examples.text: Greg Short recounts Bloom's first million-dollar day (circa 2020-2021, Brooklyn, New York). After the brand's greens powder was out of stock for a couple of weeks, Short and co-founder Mari restocked the product and simultaneously deployed every marketing channel they had: an email blast, an SMS campaign, Facebook ads, and meme page ad placements — all going live at once. Short watched the Shopify dashboard from their co-working space with just the two of them in the office. Within 12 hours, Bloom had generated $1.36 million in sales — their first million-dollar day — with roughly three people in the company.

practices.text: When restocking a product after an out-of-stock period, deploy all marketing channels (email, SMS, paid social, influencer/meme placements) simultaneously rather than sequentially, to concentrate pent-up demand into a single revenue spike.
